description: DG-6 over-decisiveness — GROUNDED partial resolution: per-battle combat-effectiveness (CEV) friction. Jordan directive 2026-07-22 ('validate emergent results top-down from historical precedent; extend code as required to resolve standing issues using academic research, military theory, mathematics, historical precedent'). Root cause CONFIRMED (mathematical): melee attrition sums N independent per-soldier dice -> CV self-averages ~1/sqrt(N) (measured 0.89->0.06 for N=4->1024); pool scales linearly with troops -> compute_degree near-deterministic from the force ratio -> outcomes collapse to 100%/0% where history shows bands. Fix (two research passes, ~200k tokens; grounding in audit/2026-07-22-mass-battle-stress-test/dg6_friction_resolution.md): keep the self-averaging attrition core, add a per-BATTLE, per-side multiplicative CEV factor M ~ LogNormal(0, sigma^2) drawn ONCE per battle (orchestration._draw_friction_cev, lazy so multi-turn re-entries keep the single draw), multiplying the subunit combat pool (core/exchange). Law of total variance: the attrition term ->0 with N (kept), the once-per-battle shock stays O(1) -> scale-invariant outcome variance (Dupuy CEV / Clausewitz friction / stochastic-Lanchester; Kingman 2002, Beyerchen 1992, Rowland, Sabin Lost Battles). CALIBRATED gauge-INDEPENDENTLY to the Dupuy DLEDB force-ratio win-curve (NOT the gauge, I5): sigma=1.1 reproduces 1.2:1->57% (t55), 1.5:1->62% (t62), 2:1->70% (t70), 3:1->82% (t80). Mechanism verified (test_friction_cev.py, 7): default-inert/byte-exact off; drawn once per battle not per turn; large-force 2:1 collapses to >=95% without friction and stays banded <90% with it (the scale-invariant-variance fix); I1/I2 hold. HONEST FINDING -- friction is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT, ships DEFAULT OFF: the 20-row history gauge moves 6/20 -> 4/20 with uniform friction ON, because (1) envelopment rows (H3/H4) stay ~100% -- their over-decisiveness is STRUCTURAL (envelopment geometry), needing a CONJUNCTIVE gate (Goldsworthy/Sabin: center-holds x cavalry-sufficiency x terrain), not symmetric noise; (2) friction BREAKS the Stage E brace repel (C2/C6 REPELLED->NOT-REPELLED: a big CEV draw lets cavalry break a braced line, but Waterloo-squares repel is near-deterministic) -- friction must be exempted/damped in the brace repel; (3) near-parity rows pushed just out of band. So it ships gated OFF (byte-exact, inert; grid oracle unaffected -- I4). Complete DG-6 resolution = (a) this CEV friction + (b) conjunctive envelopment gate + (c) brace-repel preservation -- scoped as follow-on. needs_jordan: default-flip + the (b)/(c) design calls. No constant tuned to the gauge.

title: The cell is the primitive for MORALE — aggregate-up/modulate-down, per-cell du Picq break-point, contagion; default flipped ON on measurement
summary: Executes Jordan's 2026-07-25 directive ("the cell needs to be the primitive for morale, discipline, quality, stamina, route, health, armour, facing, damage, troops count, etc") for MORALE, the first state to move. Before this the cell was the primitive for GEOMETRY only, so Jordan's own test case ("a cell should be able to have worse morale than another cell in same subunit") was not representable: a rear cell being cut down and a front cell holding shared one scalar. PHASE 1 - cells carry morale; the subunit's morale is the troop-weighted MEAN of its live cells (derived, not stored) and that holistic value pulls its own cells back toward it at a discipline-gated rate (cohere_cells, signed both ways, conserves the aggregate). Erosion scales by FRACTION of the cell, not absolute count, so dense cells are not spuriously braver. PHASE 2 - a broken cell (morale <= 0) stops contributing combat weight while its men REMAIN present and killable (a break is not a casualty event); breaks spread over the 8-neighbourhood lattice, so the spread follows the formation's own shape with no shape-specific code; a body whose broken cells hold CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC of its men is no longer a formation. PHASE 2B - the phase that made phase 2 reachable at all. Phases 1+2 measured BYTE-IDENTICAL to phase 1 across all 20 rows; instrumentation showed 72 of 144 cells 'broken' at exactly -1.0, one uniform write, i.e. cells were breaking as a CONSEQUENCE of the body routing. Root cause was an ASYMMETRY, not a magnitude: bodies get erosion AND a du Picq break-point, cells had erosion only, so a cell had to be destroyed twice over to break by erosion and the body always won that race by construction. check_cell_breaks() gives each cell its own break-point drawn in the same historical 15-30% band, discipline-skewed. FLIP - measured against a same-session flag-OFF control at n=60 in the resolving (multi) mode: win-share 7/20 -> 8/20 and casualty/duration realism 2/20 -> 7/20. The casualty column is the evidence and it is a mechanism producing a SHAPE, not a fitted number: loser losses fall out of 31-40% into 26-30% (H6 79.2 -> 48.9, C7 39.9 -> 32.1), which is du Picq's claim that a body comes apart before it is destroyed. Costs stated: single mode 7/20 -> 5/20 (both flipped rows are sub-1 sigma band-edge moves at n=60 in the mode the gauge documents as non-resolving); C4 91.5 -> 96.7 against a 95 ceiling (~0.5 sigma); reverse-pair symmetry 3.8 -> 3.4 sigma with H4/H11 still ASYMMETRIC and still open. Both byte-exact goldens RE-RECORDED (not pinned off) so the change-detector keeps tracking the shipped engine. UNPLANNED FINDING, recorded not acted on: with per-cell break-points live, PC_STOCHASTIC_ROUT is INERT in the shipped configuration - loser casualties 35.6% with it off vs 36.1% on, no separation. The cells break first and CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC ends the body before the subunit-level draw is consulted. It remains load-bearing on the unseeded fallback path, so it is a retirement CANDIDATE, not dead code. CORRECTION ON THE RECORD: I flagged an 'over-firing' signal (76-100% single-mode draw rates) from the phase-2b run. The flag-OFF control shows those same rows at 100% draws with the flag off - the pre-existing tick-cap artifact the gauge's own docstring documents. I read rows from a run with no control beside it; a number without its control is not a measurement, for a worrying number as much as a flattering one.

safety: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: PC_CELL_MORALE default OFF -> ON; both byte-exact grid goldens re-recorded and _PINNED_OFF gains PC_CELL_MORALE='1'. Fully reversible with PC_CELL_MORALE=0, which restores the scalar path verbatim (pinned by test_unseeded_is_the_scalar_path_verbatim). CELL_BREAK_ROUT_FRAC (0.5) and CELL_MORALE_PULL (0.25) are tagged CALIBRATED-DEBT: du Picq mechanism, unfitted magnitude, and now SHIPPED unfitted rather than dormant.

title: RETRACTION of the same-day PC_CELL_MORALE flip — the measurement's two arms were not comparable
summary: Supersedes the prior ED-MB-0042 entry's FLIP paragraph. The per-cell morale MECHANISM (phases 1/2/2b) stands and is unchanged; the DEFAULT FLIP and its measurement are withdrawn. CAUSE: between_turn_recovery and reset_morale_between_battles both write the morale SCALAR, which eff_morale stops reading the moment cells are seeded, so under PC_CELL_MORALE they are silent no-ops (verified directly: knock a body's cells to 2.0, call both, still 2.0). The gauge's multi mode runs multi-turn battles and resets morale between them, so the ON arm fought with morale that never recovered while the OFF arm's did. 'The loser breaks earlier' is precisely what an unrecoverable body also produces, so the reported 7->8/20 win-share and 2->7/20 casualty-realism gains cannot be attributed to the mechanism. Reverted: default OFF, _PINNED_OFF back to '0', both byte-exact goldens back to their pre-flip digests, default-pinning test restored with the reason. SAME DEFECT CLASS AS THE erode_morale SILENT NO-OP caught earlier in this same lane and session. That one was fixed as a single instance with no sweep for the pattern, so it recurred and this time reached a shipped default and a golden re-record. The transferable lesson is about the UNIT OF REPAIR: when a defect's cause is 'a representation change orphaned its writers', the repair is every writer, found by grep, not the writer that happened to fail. TWO GENUINE DEFECTS FOUND BY THE FAILING SUITE AND KEPT, both real bugs in the phase-1/2b work and independent of the flip: (1) BORN-BROKEN SUBUNITS — seed_cell_morale ran in Subunit.__post_init__, but a subunit with morale=None inherits from its parent Unit and the _unit back-ref is not set until Unit.__post_init__, strictly later; so an inheriting subunit seeded every cell at eff_morale's no-parent fallback of 0, i.e. born broken, emitting no combat weight and unable to recover because once cells exist eff_morale reads THEM and never falls back to the correct parent scalar. Inheriting subunits are now seeded from Unit.__post_init__. The gauge path passes morale explicitly, which is why the targeted tests and the measurement were green while ten unrelated suite tests were not. (2) A 1-ULP AGGREGATE DEFEATING AN IDENTITY — the troop-weighted mean of N equal values is that value mathematically but not in floats (15 cells at 6.0 -> 5.999999999999999); _morale_sigma divides by morale_start, so a body at full morale reported sigma -1.8e-16 instead of 0, enough to cross a DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE boundary and turn a 6.0 exchange into 0.0. A uniform body now returns its cells' value exactly. My own t=0 identity test HID this by asserting with pytest.approx — the one assertion form that cannot see an ulp; it now asserts ==. BLOCKER for re-flipping is the scalar-write sweep, not another gauge run. Known sites: between_turn_recovery (unit + atom), reset_morale_between_battles (unit + atom), the rout write u.morale = 0.0, Unit.erode_morale, and core/state.py's atom.morale = atom.eff_morale.
provenance: Direct verification of the no-op (probe on between_turn_recovery / reset_morale_between_battles under PC_CELL_MORALE=1); 10 suite failures on the flipped default; git-recovered pre-flip golden digests
safety: NET BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IS ZERO in the shipped configuration: PC_CELL_MORALE is back to its pre-session default of OFF and both goldens are back to their pre-flip digests, so the engine ships exactly as it did before the flip. The two kept fixes are reachable only under the flag, which is off.
follow_on: Scalar-write sweep is the BLOCKER and is tracked as its own work item (a fresh ED on allocation), not as this entry's open state: this entry's own action -- the retraction -- is complete. Scalar-write sweep (route every .morale assignment through the cells when seeded), THEN re-measure the flag honestly, THEN decide the flip. Phases 3 (stamina/discipline/quality, retires col_grid) and 4 (hp/armour) remain unbuilt. test_per_cell_break_subsumes_the_body_level_one's absolute figures were taken under the same no-recovery confound — its OFF-vs-ON comparison is still fair (both arms share the confound) but its 35.6/36.1 absolutes must be re-taken after the sweep.

title: Same-side cell exclusion (PC_CELL_EXCLUSION, default ON): inter-subunit deep overlap -48.6%, cross-side -74.4% -- and the deadlock it shipped with
description: Jordan 2026-07-29: 'We need to prevent inter-subunit collisions', with the design steer 'we are using a field system so there shouldn't even be any assignment issues so long as cell boundaries are respected.' resolve_toi_and_commit's own docstring already states the invariant -- 'two unit squares that must never interpenetrate' -- but applied it to CROSS-SIDE pairs only, so a cell of one subunit walked through a cell of another on its own side. This adds the same swept-SAT body-box solve to same-side pairs. No new mechanism, no RNG, no third definition of 'these two bodies touch'. || THE DEFECT IT FIRST SHIPPED WITH, and the more instructive half. It accepted a time-of-impact of s == 0.0, copying the cross-side loop, where that is a safe defensive floor because armies start apart and pre-existing contact is caught upstream by halted_cells. Same-side pairs invert every one of those assumptions: the formation lattice has pitch 1.0 and the bodies are 1.0x1.0, so every adjacent cell in every formation is touching BY CONSTRUCTION and permanently, and no cell is ever halted against its own neighbour. MEASURED: 568,785 of 1,213,199 same-side solves -- 46.9% -- returned exactly 0.0, against 9.84% cross-side. Halted cells FELL 20,356 -> 3,300; resolve calls ROSE 1,482 -> 11,934. Frozen formations never close, never contact, never halt, so every battle ran to the turn cap. That 8.05x TICK inflation was the entire '8.2x slowdown' (47s -> 386s) the pass was blamed for -- which is why a swept-AABB broad phase written to fix the COST bought nothing (386s -> 370s): it culled pairs correctly inside a loop whose ITERATION COUNT was the defect. Broad phase removed; runtime now 1.41x baseline. The rule is s > 0 and introduces no constant: capping at s == 0.0 cannot un-overlap a pre-existing overlap, it freezes the pair where it already sits for zero corrective benefit and total motion cost. || RESULT, on deep overlap (obb_overlap AND penetration depth >= 0.1; the raw boolean is dominated by the lattice's permanent tangency and over-states the defect ~10x): inter-subunit 13,477 -> 6,932 (-48.6%), cross-side 875 -> 224 (-74.4%), same-subunit 43,068 -> 44,531 (+3.4%). NOT zero, for two identified reasons: the rule deliberately skips pairs already overlapping at tick start and nothing in the engine ever separates them (resolve_internal_collisions, ED-MB-0057, is the only primitive built for that and is intra-subunit + grid-era); and the whole solve is gated on toi_deferred = FIELD_MOVEMENT and enemy_cells_float, so formations with no enemy supplied still interpenetrate freely -- same-side exclusion inherits a cross-side precondition it has no reason to. || COST, measured with a control (§0.1 #4): the pass suppresses contact and therefore casualties. Mean end-state hp over all 20 historical rows at t=24 rose 0.8684 -> 0.8939, i.e. total attrition fell 19%, on a casualty model already flagged as far too low. Shipped ON per the standing 'gate models ON' directive with the cost recorded rather than discovered later. || GOLDENS: unit_field 6f594233 -> 0194efcc, cell_field 2a9214eb -> da6d685e. ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: re-running at PC_CELL_EXCLUSION=0 reproduces BOTH previous goldens byte-for-byte, so 100% of the delta is this pass and nothing else in the changeset; both grid modes byte-identical with the flag ON. GUARD: tests/valoria/test_cell_exclusion_no_deadlock.py, mutation-verified -- dropping the s <= 0.0 skip freezes the fixture dead (0 cells moved between tick 1 and tick 6).

title: RETRACTION: both published co-location figures were wrong, in opposite directions -- the second was a confounded arm
description: Corrects ED-MB-0056 and an unpublished intermediate. RETRACTED #1: '17.31% overlap rate' was ROUNDED-SQUARE co-location -- cell positions int(round())-ed onto a lattice and counted as collisions when they shared a square. The field path is continuous; two bodies 0.6 apart round into a collision that never happened. It over-counts. RETRACTED #2, the worse one: '17.31% -> 0.35% with exclusion ON' was measured on an arm where the exclusion pass had DEADLOCKED the engine (ED-MB-0059) -- cells were not overlapping because they were not moving. That is the §0.1 confound exactly: an uncontrolled measurement banked because it was favourable, and the adversarial pass run on it attacked the number rather than the setup, which is the specific failure §0.1 was written after. || THE CORRECTED INSTRUMENT: audit/2026-07-29-scenario-visualization/measure_colocation.py, now a tracked standing probe rather than an ad-hoc script (being ad-hoc is how both figures went out unchecked). It reports body-box interpenetration via geometry.obb_overlap -- the engine's existing single owner of 'these two bodies overlap', not a fourth definition -- THRESHOLDED BY PENETRATION DEPTH. Depth is load-bearing: the lattice pitch is 1.0 and the bodies are 1.0x1.0, so _sat_separated's documented boundary (centre distance exactly 1.0 counts as separated) means neighbours sit EXACTLY ON the predicate's boundary by construction and any sub-millimetre jitter flips it. Measured at t=4: of 16,847 overlapping same-subunit pairs the MEDIAN depth is 0.0029 lattice units and 88.5% are below 0.1; only ~295 (1.8%) exceed 0.5. A raw overlap boolean over-states the defect by roughly an order of magnitude, in the same way the rounded-square metric over-states it in the other direction. || A hypothesis was also raised and FALSIFIED en route, recorded so it is not re-raised: that same-subunit overlap was an artefact of per-cell facing rotation (a rotated unit square's circumscribed radius is 0.707 > 0.5, so any relative rotation at pitch 1.0 must interpenetrate). 100% of overlapping pairs measured have IDENTICAL facing. The Euclidean-distance discriminator used to test it was itself wrong for boxes -- two aligned squares at diagonal offset (0.8, 0.8) are 1.13 apart and still overlap.

description: Executes Jordan's 2026-08-01 ruling on ED-MB-0061 SS5 fork 1: 'if they are distinctly different items, then rename by distinction accordingly with cells reserved for mass battle'. BRANCH 1 APPLIES, adjudicated on evidence: the two things sharing 'cell' are distinct — PER_CELL is the mass-battle GEOMETRY primitive (resolution granularity; keeps the name per the ruling) and PC_CELL_MORALE is per-cell MORALE, a state-ownership flag that merely also operates on cells. Not overlapping (branch 2) and not a scale-transition problem needing a wrapper (branch 3). THE DEFECT WAS SUFFIX-ON-TRUE, AND IT IS WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT. _mode_key was ALREADY injective — all 8 cube points mapped to 8 distinct strings — so the existing injectivity pin passed. The key was RELATIVE, not ambiguous: a suffix appeared only when a flag was ON, so absence encoded 'OFF' only relative to the default at recording time. 'cell' never meant 'cell-morale off'; it meant 'cell-morale not mentioned'. Flip PC_CELL_MORALE's default to 1 — which the flags-ON directive (ED-MB-0001) requires — and the plain grid run starts keying cell_cm and checks itself against the fifth mode's golden, while unit / cell / unit_field / cell_field become strings no run can ever emit. FIX: keys are absolute — <geometry>_<movement>_<morale>, every axis present WITH ITS VALUE. unit->unit_grid_mor0, cell->cell_grid_mor0, unit_field->unit_field_mor0, cell_field->cell_field_mor0, cell_cm->cell_grid_mor1. At PC_CELL_MORALE=1 a run now keys *_mor1 and reports MISSING honestly instead of matching a different configuration's golden. NO DIGESTS CHANGED — this renames lookup KEYS only; every recorded value carried across byte-for-byte, so it is NOT a golden re-record and G11 does not apply. VERIFIED: the run emits 'DIGEST unit_grid_mor0 ccdf7d09...' against the same recorded 241f04e5... it did before (the pre-existing F-series drift, unchanged), and cell_field_mor0 STILL MATCHES its golden under the new key — a mis-mapped migration would have broken that. CONSEQUENCE: this is what makes the all-flags-ON re-base RECORDABLE. The re-base was blocked because there was no stable name for the ON configurations; there now is, and three (unit_grid_mor1, unit_field_mor1, cell_field_mor1) are correctly reported as awaiting a recording rather than silently colliding. ED-MB-0061 SS4.2's Phase 0 can proceed.

description: TRACK-F / F2 DIAGNOSED AND CLOSED: 'rear damage 0.0' was a CONFOUNDED TEST, not an engine regression. HANDOFF_MB recorded F2 as 'NOT PC_FACING_MODEL -- it survives that flag being off, cause unknown'. A full single-flag bisect over every boolean in tests/sim/mass_battle/config.py fingered PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL as the only flag whose OFF state restores the pass -- and that answer is WRONG, which is the substance of this entry. MEASURED CAUSAL CHAIN (tests/valoria/test_octagon_damage.py::test_rear_is_exactly_double_front, seed 5): the two arms flipped the defender's advance_dir between -1 and +1 while the docstring claimed 'same dice, same contact cells, only the facing arc differs'. advance_dir orients the whole SUBUNIT, so the arms contacted DIFFERENT cells of B -- rank (0,*) in the front arm vs rank (2,*) in the rear arm, measured in the original frame via cells_to_orig_coords. Different cells carry different troops, so B's own pool moved 3.6 -> 1.333 between arms. compute_degree is RELATIVE, so the smaller pool rolling well (net 2) outranked the larger one (net 1): A's IDENTICAL net of 1.0 read 'Success' in the front arm and 'Partial' in the rear. DAMAGE_BY_DEGREE['Partial'] is 1, minus the universal dr=1, equals 0.0 -- a rear strike doing less than a frontal one. The arc multiplier was never mis-applied. WHY THE BISECT LIES: PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL=0 floors 3.6 -> 3 and 1.333 -> 1, which at this seed happens to keep B's net under A's. It MASKS the confound; it does not cause it. Recording it as F2's cause would have shipped a wrong diagnosis that reproduces on demand -- the failure mode CLAUDE.md 0.1 #4 names, since a flag flip that changes a result is not a control. TWO HYPOTHESES REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE THIRD WAS CONFIRMED, both recorded because each looked correct: (a) roll_pool_fractional consumes a random draw CONDITIONALLY (random.random() < frac), so the arms' RNG streams should diverge -- refuted, both arms drew exactly 2; (b) support_engage_frac reads cells in the ORIGINAL frame, so a rear-contacted subunit should lose its support stack -- refuted, engage_frac measured 1.0 in both arms. FIX: a new _arc_pair helper holds the defender's BODY FIXED at advance_dir=-1 and rotates only cell_facing_vec, via the def_face parameter that already existed in _dmg_b and was DEAD -- the hook for the correct isolation was present and unused. Measured across the 12 seeds at shipped defaults (PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL ON): 7 exact 2.0x, 0 violations. The two exact-ratio tests (test_rear_is_exactly_double_front, test_rear_penalty_persists_across_reaction_window) now route through it; test_front_takes_no_arc_penalty is left alone because it asserts an INEQUALITY that survives the confound, and moving a passing test buys nothing. FALSIFIER (0.1 #3): mutation-verified 3/3 -- OCTAGON_DMG_MULT RED 2.0->1.0 kills 3 tests, RED 2.0->2.5 kills 2, YELLOW 1.5->1.0 kills 2. The suite observes the multiplier rather than passing vacuously. config.py restored byte-exact after each mutant (git diff empty). NO GOLDEN WAS RE-RECORDED. This closes F2 by fixing the measurement, not by moving the expectation -- the ordering HANDOFF_MB's Track-F plan requires ('bisect each failure -> fix F1-F8 -> rule the mode matrix -> re-base ONCE'). Jordan's mode-matrix ruling landed as ED-MB-0062; F1/F3-F8 still need their own bisects before any re-base.

CORRECTION ROW (append-only; supersedes the earlier ED-MB-0063 row on three points). An independent read-only critic pass ran against the committed claims and refuted part of them. The headline finding -- F2 is a confounded TEST, not an engine regression -- SURVIVES and was independently re-derived. Three things were wrong and are corrected here rather than quietly edited, because the errors are more instructive than the result. (1) THE STATED CAUSE WAS WRONG. The earlier row said the pool moved 3.6 -> 1.333 because 'different cells carry different troops'. FALSE: Subunit.distribution defaults to 'uniform', so every cell holds troop_count/len(ids) and ranks 0 and 2 are identical in troops. The real mechanism is SUPPORT DEPTH, in core/exchange.py::_pair_engaged_troops: front_r = min(r) over the contact cells, and deeper cells are credited at SUPPORT_WEIGHTS {1:1.0, 2:0.7, 3:0.5}. Contacting rank 0 leaves two ranks behind it -> (5 + 5*1.0 + 5*0.7)/15 = 0.9 of base; contacting rank 2 leaves none -> 5/15 = 1/3. At base pool 4 that reproduces 3.6 and 1.3333 to the digit. (2) THE 'REFUTED' HYPOTHESIS WAS CORRECT IN CONCEPT AND DISMISSED ON THE WRONG FUNCTION. The earlier row recorded support-stack loss as refuted by measuring geometry.support_engage_frac at 1.0 in both arms. That function is NEVER CALLED on this path -- orchestration.py guards it with `if POOL_VARIANT != "C-ii"` and POOL_VARIANT == 'C-ii' -- and its min(1.0, ...) cap would have hidden the asymmetry regardless. So the right idea was discarded by pattern-matching a NAME instead of following the live path, and a wrong idea was adopted in its place. Both the failed refutation and the retro-fitted explanation passed my own adversarial pass and were caught only by a structurally independent reader; that is the argument for the relay, not a footnote to it. (3) THE FALSIFIER WAS OVERSTATED: 2/3, NOT 3/3. OCTAGON_DMG_MULT['YELLOW'] has NO readers anywhere -- the only live read is ['RED'] (orchestration.py:1316) and the flank value is INTERPOLATED (mult = 1 - arc*(RED-1)/2), never looked up. Re-run cleanly with a count assertion: the YELLOW 1.5 -> 1.0 mutant kills NOTHING (6/6 pass). The earlier '3/3 mutants killed' was wrong, and a wrong falsifier is worse than none, because 0.1 #3 makes the artifact the evidence. RED 2.0 -> 1.0 (kills 3) and RED 2.0 -> 2.5 (kills 2) stand. Side finding, worth its own look: the YELLOW constant is dead config. (4) PRIOR ART NOT CREDITED. audit/2026-07-30-mb-session-retrospective/00_lessons.md had ALREADY classified F2 as a test-premise defect and named orig-frame support depth. The earlier row presented the diagnosis as fresh. It is an implementation of that classification, not a discovery -- and the correct mechanism was sitting 14 lines below the bisect table that was quoted from the same document. STRONGER FALSIFIER ADDED (critic finding D). '7 of 12 seeds gave exactly 2.0x' is near-vacuous: once the body is held fixed both arms share one RNG stream and the ratio is arithmetically forced. The new test_arc_ratio_is_invariant_to_the_fractional_pool_flag parametrizes PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL over both settings, which is the property that was FALSE before (ON failed, OFF passed -- the flag-dependence that DEFINED F2). Mutation-verified by reintroducing the def_adv +/-1 confound: it fails on [1] and passes on [0], reproducing F2's exact signature. The fixture now also pins PC_FRACTIONAL_POOL explicitly instead of inheriting the ambient default. RECORDED, NOT FIXED (critic findings A/B/C, all pre-existing): A -- test_rear_penalty_persists_across_reaction_window does NOT traverse the window it names. The reaction counter is consecutive-tick in a per-subunit map, _arc_pair builds a FRESH Subunit per call, so _cnt can never exceed 1 while FACING_REACTION_TICKS is 2; the wheel branch is unreachable and an engine that DID wheel would still pass. Varying t varies the tick LABEL, not elapsed time. The correct form ticks a persistent subunit, as test_visible_flank_refuses_after_delay already does in the same file. Noted in the docstring so routing it through _arc_pair does not imply a validation that did not happen. B -- test_front_takes_no_arc_penalty still uses the def_adv +/-1 pairing. Justifying that as 'an inequality that survives the confound' is a structural claim with no control, which is the shape this entry exists to condemn. Left in place, flagged. C -- the isolation is scenario-dependent, not structural: cell_facing_vec also feeds _per_cell_angle_mod (charge-shock, envelopment-shock, brace-recoil) and _compute_atom_sides, inert only because this fixture has no brace, no momentum differential, one subunit per side. Stated in the docstring so the precondition is not silently inherited -- which is exactly how the original confound was inherited. SCOPE OF THE 8 -> 7 SUITE FIGURE: local full `pytest tests/valoria` on this branch, NOT the 16-local/17-CI baseline HANDOFF_MB quotes at 94bb902, which was a different tree and flag set. The two are not reconciled and should not be read as the same measurement.

description: GOVERNANCE REPAIR -- registers Jordan's 2026-08-03 canon-tree ruling (J2), which until now existed ONLY in audit/2026-08-03-session-oddities.md:163-164 and a commit message. Zero register hits: CURRENT.md still listed the two-disjoint-code-trees fork among 'Findings held for Jordan' (the 2026-07-26 ED-MB-0043 stamp), and ED-MB-0043's follow_on (b) 'which tree is the port oracle' was still open with needs_jordan true. A session following the repo's own priority order (CURRENT.md > a PROPOSED proposal) would therefore CORRECTLY have concluded the fork was still open -- while tools/build_fork.py:16-17 and its CARRY row :53-54 simultaneously asserted 'tests/sim/mass_battle/ (28 modules) is CANON per ED-MB-0043' as settled fact and :20 called the swap 'an open decision'. Three surfaces, three different states, no register. THE RULING: canon mass battle is tests/sim/mass_battle/ (28 modules, 11,269 LOC, all 12 PC_* flag files). The 5-module systems/mass_battle/sim/ tree the campaign currently imports is RETIRED, not kept alongside. This CLOSES ED-MB-0043 follow_on (b). SCOPE LIMIT, stated because the prior draft over-read it: J2 settles WHICH ENGINE and does NOT author `degree`. Canon has no four-band degree; it must be authored, and audit/2026-08-03-session-oddities.md section H is the shape record -- note H supersedes the widely-copied '{winner, turns, phases}' return, which was read off the kind='single' path; the caller uses kind='multi', returning {winner, battle_turns, log, a_loss_final, b_loss_final}. PARTIAL PROGRESS ON degree (Jordan, 2026-08-04): mass battle is to occur ON A MAP, and the loser of the scene is whoever loses more units or has their settlement captured. That supplies the winner/loser rule the adapter's attacker_wins mapping needed and constrains the band ladder to a unit-differential/objective-capture basis; it does not by itself fix the four band edges, so the degree_map remains a required-argument-with-no-default per keys.py:27-30's precedent until the bands are ruled. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RE-HOME: under the keep-main direction (see ED-IN-0125) the tests/sim/mass_battle -> systems/mass_battle/canon move is an in-repo `git mv`, not a copy, so history survives via --follow and the ci_co_file_checker rule-3 misfire on canon-engine edits (A3) dies at its source rather than being worked around.
